name: Precigen, Inc.

profile.description: Precigen (formerly Intrexon, renamed January 2020) is a Germantown, Maryland gene and cell therapy company built on platforms including AdenoVerse gene delivery, UltraCAR-T, RheoSwitch and ActoBiotics. Its first commercial product, PAPZIMEOS for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, is driving a steep launch ramp: Q2 2026 PAPZIMEOS net revenue of $53.1M more than doubled from $21.6M in Q1, total Q2 revenue reached $55.0M (vs ~$0.9M a year earlier), and the company reported its first quarterly profit ($20.1M net income). FY2025 revenue was $9.7M with a $250.6M net loss.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Precigen transformed itself from Intrexon's sprawling synthetic-biology conglomerate into a focused gene therapy company in 2020 [3], then took PAPZIMEOS from development to a commercial launch generating $74.7M of net revenue in H1 2026, with Q2 sales of $53.1M more than doubling Q1 [2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or quantified AI efficiencies were found. Market Share (1/2): PAPZIMEOS is gaining rapid adoption in recurrent respiratory papillomatosis [2], but no market-share data was found to confirm category leadership. Pipeline (1/2): The AdenoVerse, UltraCAR-T and ActoBiotics platforms support further programs [5], but no specific next-gen launches with dates were found. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $40.1M was over 4x revenue of $9.7M [1].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Precigen describes itself as dedicated to discovering and developing gene and cell therapies to improve patients' lives [5] — clear about what it does but not distinctive among biotechs. Community Impact (0/2): No foundation or community program with cited dollar amounts was found. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data found for its ~160 employees. Insider Buying (0/2): No net open-market insider buying identified; the company relied on equity and warrant financing, with weighted shares rising from 167M (2020) to 305M (2025) [1].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored (Growth sleeve). D/E 225.7% (0.32) [6]; ROE -837% (0.0, 2x) [6]; revenue growth YoY +6,323% as PAPZIMEOS sales lapped a near-zero base (1.0) [6][2]; 5-yr revenue CAGR -21.3% derived from FMP FY2020 $32.0M to FY2025 $9.7M (0.0, 2x) [1]; forward P/E -30.2 is negative (0.0) [6]; profit margin -184% TTM (0.0) [6]. Forward PEG excluded (null) because it is not meaningful on negative earnings (FMP's 0.05 reading is an artifact). Weighted sum 1.32/8 = 1.65 → 2. Liquidity cleared: 5.23M shares x $6.64 = ~$34.7M/day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Precigen's value lies in FDA-approved, manufactured biologics (PAPZIMEOS) and proprietary gene-delivery platforms [2][5] — regulated, physical-world products that AI cannot substitute; no analyst commentary flags AI displacement. The residual risk is indirect: AI-accelerated drug discovery could compress the time for competitors to bring rival therapies to its indications. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue or AI products were found.

infinite_game.summary: Precigen's defining act was existential: abandoning Intrexon's scattered bets across agriculture, energy and animal science to focus on gene therapy, then shepherding PAPZIMEOS to market. That required courage and flexibility Sinek would respect. But its cause remains a generic biotech mission, years of dilution and a 2020-era shareholder litigation history weigh on trust, and the company is only now proving it can stand on its own revenue.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The stated dedication to gene and cell therapies for patients [5] is sincere but interchangeable with peers; no evidence it has been articulated as a vision that shapes sacrifices beyond the normal biotech mission.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Helen Sabzevari, who joined in 2017, has led the company since the January 2020 refocus, providing leadership continuity [3]. No Glassdoor or retention data was found to show exceptional trust, and past investor investigations over methane-bioconversion disclosures [4] point to an earlier era of governance strain.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors' strengths or framing competition as a driver of self-improvement; messaging centers on the company's own launch metrics [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): The company fundamentally reinvented itself — renaming from Intrexon to Precigen and refocusing on healthcare in 2020 [3], and divesting non-core units (FY2022 includes $108M of income from discontinued operations) [1] — abandoning the legacy synthetic-biology conglomerate model to become a commercial gene therapy company.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership kept funding R&D ($40-53M per year from 2022-2025) through a long period of minimal revenue and mounting losses to reach commercialization [1], a costly long-term bet that is now paying off with Q2 2026 profitability [2]. The bet was financed by heavy dilution rather than sacrifice by insiders.

investment_thesis: PAPZIMEOS is one of the steeper biotech launches in recent memory: net revenue went from $21.6M in Q1 2026 to $53.1M in Q2, total Q2 revenue was $55.0M versus about $0.9M a year earlier, and Precigen posted its first quarterly profit of $20.1M [2]. At a ~$2.4B market cap [6], continued uptake in recurrent respiratory papillomatosis could quickly grow into the valuation, while the AdenoVerse and UltraCAR-T platforms offer additional shots on goal [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is concentration and balance-sheet quality. Precigen is effectively a single-product company, and management itself cautioned that launch growth rates diminish as a launch matures [2]. FY2025 net loss was $250.6M including large non-operating charges, D/E is ~226%, ROE is deeply negative, and the share count nearly doubled from 2020 to 2025 [1][6]. The five-year revenue trend is -21% CAGR after divestitures [1], Sustainalytics-type ESG risk ratings sit in the high-risk band (~37) [4], and any payer pushback or competing therapy could stall the ramp.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results showing whether PAPZIMEOS revenue keeps compounding beyond Q2's $53.1M and profitability is sustained [2]
Broader payer coverage and patient uptake in recurrent respiratory papillomatosis driving FY2026 revenue far above FY2025's $9.7M [2][1]
Advancement or partnering of AdenoVerse/UltraCAR-T pipeline assets, funded by PAPZIMEOS cash flow [5]
key_risks: Single-product dependence: a slowdown in PAPZIMEOS uptake would undercut the entire thesis, as management flagged decelerating launch growth over time [2]
Leverage and dilution: D/E ~226% and weighted shares up from 167M to 305M over five years [6][1]
Governance overhang from prior shareholder litigation over Intrexon-era disclosures and high-risk ESG ratings [4]
